question: What universal maximum service life, in years, does the MUTCD assign to every traffic sign before mandatory replacement?
model_answer: Direct Answer: The MUTCD does not assign a universal maximum service life in years to traffic signs, and none of the evidence provided contains any such provision. The evidence supplied concerns sign sizes, placement locations, and general purposes — not sign replacement intervals. The question rests on a premise the MUTCD (as evidenced here) does not support; sign maintenance and replacement are handled through condition- and retroreflectivity-based practices rather than a fixed age limit, but no provision on that topic appears in the evidence either. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows Table 2H-1, which lists General Information sign and plaque sizes, not service life. [Image 2] (Figure 2A-2) illustrates heights and lateral locations of sign installations, with no service-life content. [Image 3] (Figure 2A-3) shows example sign locations at intersections, unrelated to replacement intervals. [Image 4] (Figure 2A-4) is a locator figure for sign chapters, with no service-life content. [Images 5–8] are page views showing tables of contents, sign design figures, and sign layout figures, none of which mention a maximum service life. Citations: - Section 1A.01 Support §1 (p.1) - Table 2H-1 (p.460) - Figure 2A-2 (p.51) - Figure 2A-3 (p.52) The evidence is insufficient to identify any mandatory sign replacement age, because no such requirement exists in the provided material.
gold_answer: The MUTCD does not specify this information. A correct response should state that the requested value or requirement cannot be determined from the manual rather than inventing an answer.
